status_reason: The paper's design is kept whole: ten 10-cube arm objects with three right-angled elbows in two mirror-image sets of five, 18 views in 20-degree steps with 7 kept per object, 400 unique 'same' pairs (20 depth and 20 picture-plane at each of 0-180 degrees) and 400 mirror 'different' pairs each shown twice, blocks of 200, a 0.5 s warning, 9 degrees spacing, 4-5 cm drawings at about 60 cm, and a speeded two-choice RT; what changed is apparatus (generated shapes instead of the unavailable originals, a monitor instead of cards, keys instead of levers, a visual warning instead of the tone), each listed as a deviation, and every unstated value is marked ASSUMED.

original.citation: Shepard, R. N., & Metzler, J. (1971). Mental rotation of three-dimensional objects. Science, 171(3972), 701-703.
original.experiments: The single experiment of the paper: same/different judgements of 1600 pairs per subject, picture-plane and depth rotations, 0-180 degrees

assets.what: 70 perspective line drawings of 10 generated arm objects (PNG) and manifest.json

notes: Software verification only (tests and simulated sessions); no participant data has been recorded with this folder.
